cells.tense: You're the one deciding what gets handed down, and you know it — the pen is in your hand right now.
cells.verb: Finishing what you set out to make, and letting it stand.
cells.place: In the shared meaning you and others keep alive together.
cells.ask: Offer one more piece than feels safe — let what you've already built feed the next thing rather than closing the account.
cells.core:
You're the one deciding what gets handed down, and you know it. The structure is standing — not nearly done, not almost there, standing — and it got that way because you kept choosing where to aim when it would have been easier to stop. What's in front of people now carries your direction in it, which is why it holds up when you're not in the room.

This is the completion face of the whole thing: the will that started as a seed is now a form others can walk into. You built it on purpose, over time, without needing anyone to watch.
cells.sheetLine: You finish what you set out to make, and it stands on its own.

cells.tense: You're already living past the end — somewhere ahead of now there's a version where it's finally done and everyone finally sees it.
cells.verb: Pushing completion forward, ahead of when it's ready to arrive.
cells.place: In the shared meaning you're trying to force into its final shape.
cells.ask: Let one thing stay unfinished, and let someone tell you what they see in it — knowing that keeps deepening rather than a verdict to nail down today.
cells.core:
You're racing a finish line that keeps moving because you keep moving it. Every conversation about what you're building becomes a chance to prove it's further along than it is — to get the recognition now, before the thing has actually earned it. The push is costing you the thing the push was for: something you could rest inside instead of something you keep defending.

What you're actually hungry for is someone to receive what you've made. That's a different motion than making them see it.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing it to be finished faster than it can finish.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you already walked through — the work behind you, and you haven't turned around to look at it.
cells.verb: Not claiming what you've already completed.
cells.place: In the shared meaning you no longer believe you belong to.
cells.ask: Find one thing you made that lasted and let yourself be seen standing next to it — shining because you are, not to prove you are.
cells.core:
There's something you finished, or nearly finished, that you talk about like it was never really yours — like you were just passing through while it happened. You stopped short of taking your place in what you already made. The completion happened; the standing-in-it didn't.

What's missing isn't more effort. It's the plain seeing of what you actually did, without flinching away from the credit.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it and never let yourself stand in it.

cells.tense: The pen is down and you're still writing — the thing you're carrying is shaping what gets passed on without you noticing you're the one carrying it.
cells.verb: Carrying a legacy you haven't called yours.
cells.place: In the shared meaning you're quietly setting around other people.
cells.ask: Say "this is mine" about one thing you've been calling everybody's — the direction you actually chose, in your own voice, once.
cells.core:
You're already the one deciding what this group carries forward — which stories get retold, which ways of doing things survive, what people call just how we are. But you talk about it like it arrived on its own, a tradition you inherited rather than one you're steering. That steering is happening every day. Saying so hasn't.

What you're doing is real and it's yours. Naming that isn't vanity. It's the difference between leading something and being haunted by it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping what survives. You just haven't said so.
